doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Not singing For the Love of Ivy at the Academy Awards
summary: Abbey Lincoln sang the song she recorded, which hurt her; John Levy tried to help.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: You recorded the soundtrack, but she sang . . .

She sang. I mean, that was her option. She was the star. Of course, she blew it, you know. She told me it took maybe thirty years, but she said, ―You should have sung that song.‖ I wanted to sing it. That hurt me. I think I cried for two weeks.
What awards ceremony, just to be clear?

Yeah, it was the Academy Awards. Yeah. But John was there for that. He tried, and I didn‘t know until later. He pulled every trick he knew how to try to get me in there to do that. But she was the star of the show. She chose to sing it, and when I look at this . . . oh, I looked at the thing. I was crying, and she was . . . I was really hurt by it all. Oh no, you know, I‘ve had it good. I didn‘t pound the pavement, so to speak, because doors would just kind of open for me, because I went in, I mean, one opening and met Quincy and Miles, and John Levy. See, then I knew all those old musicians because John had made sure that they would come and see me, and meet me and stuff.
